summary: The headline linkage-rate arithmetic is traceable, but the draft overstates what its genealogical-link validation establishes: it validates some links, not transcription accuracy, and most added links remain unverifiable. The most important fix is to narrow the abstract and conclusion from “genuine accuracy improvements” to the specific observed increases in verified links, while adding reproducible code for the currently untraceable model-performance and legibility statistics.

findings.title: Validation of linked pairs is presented as proof of genuine transcription accuracy
findings.what_the_code_does: The included validation tables classify a linked pair as verified or contradicted only by comparison with a FamilySearch genealogical link. The paper itself states that a link outside that reference set is `unverifiable` and that directly contradicted links are only a lower bound on incorrect links. It then expressly acknowledges at lines 646-650 that this exercise validates links, while validation of the transcriptions themselves has not been completed.
findings.why_it_matters: The abstract and introduction claim “genuine accuracy improvements rather than spurious matches,” but the evidence establishes only that the count and share of links confirmed by the available reference set increase. It cannot determine the accuracy of the machine transcription, and it cannot rule out errors among the large unverifiable category—for example, 1,460,694 of the 2,804,662 new exact-name target-sample links are unverifiable. This is the paper’s central accuracy claim and is likely to draw a referee objection.
findings.how_to_check: Using the link-level validation output, tabulate `verified`, `contradicted`, and `unverifiable` separately for old and new links, including added links alone. Then restrict to reference-covered people and calculate `verified/(verified+contradicted)`. Confirm that no transcription string is compared with an independently adjudicated name; the draft already states this at lines 646-650.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace claims of demonstrated transcription accuracy and absence of spurious matches with the narrower result: verified-link counts rise and the contradicted share falls under the available, incomplete reference standard. Reserve transcription-accuracy claims for the planned blinded or profile-name validation and clearly state that unverifiable links prevent ruling out false positives overall.

findings.title: The four out-of-sample model-performance percentages have no producing code in the repository
findings.what_the_code_does: The paper reports whole-name and character agreement of 97.38%, 98.61%, 94.54%, and 98.29%. The closest repository preparation code retains complete records with `keep if namelast!="" & namefrst!="" & namefrst_fs!="" & namelast_fs!="" & age!=. & age_fs!=.` and saves a label dataset. No file under `CODE/` implements the claimed agreement restriction, 10% split, model training, prediction scoring, sequence metric, token denominator, or the four reported values.
findings.why_it_matters: These are the paper’s only direct out-of-sample transcription-performance measurements. Their test-set construction, treatment of padding and missing predictions, and reported percentages cannot be checked against executable source.
findings.how_to_check: Run `rg -n "97\\.38|98\\.61|94\\.54|98\\.29|sequence accuracy|token accuracy" CODE`. Identify the prediction-level test data and run the missing scoring program to reproduce all four cells and their denominators.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the frozen test predictions and a self-contained scoring script that constructs the stated test sample, asserts train/test separation, defines character denominators and missing-output treatment, and writes the LaTeX table directly.

findings.title: The national low-legibility statistics are not calculated by the active all-state analysis
findings.what_the_code_does: The active all-state script collapses outcomes by enumeration district and runs `binsreg l legibility` and `binsreg v legibility`; it never defines legibility quartiles or computes the quoted 46.2%, 14.0%, 16.9%, 27.7%, 20.3%, 28.1%, or “up to 35 percent” results. The repository’s only `lowest_quartile_leg=legibility<=r(p25)` calculation is inside a commented-out block built from the Rhode Island dataset, and its commands do not compute the displayed national values.
findings.why_it_matters: The introduction and results present precise national heterogeneity findings that cannot be traced to the figure generator. The 35% claim also sits uneasily beside the later stated 20% lowest-quartile gain, without code showing what population or point generates 35%.
findings.how_to_check: After line 221 of `create_figures_SSHA2025.do`, calculate ED-level quartiles, tabulate mean disagreement and linkage rates in the lowest and highest quartiles before and after transcription, and record whether EDs or people are weighted. Compare those outputs with every value at paper lines 739-740 and identify the observation or bin underlying 35%.
findings.suggested_fix: Add active all-state code that calculates and exports the quartile statistics from the same sample used in the plotted figure. State the weighting rule and replace the prose values, including 35%, if they do not reproduce exactly.

findings.title: The headline-results input imposes an undisclosed FamilySearch-age completeness restriction
findings.what_the_code_does: The stated producer of `census1940_all_labeled_data.dta` retains observations only when all four names and both ages are present: `... & age!=. & age_fs!=.`. The headline script reads that file and later applies `age>=10`. The paper instead defines the analysis sample by the four name fields and attributes the headline table’s smaller count solely to subsequent socio-demographic and link-file merges.
findings.why_it_matters: If any otherwise eligible record lacks `age_fs`, it is removed before the merges discussed in the table note. The reported headline sample therefore has an additional selection rule not disclosed in the sample definition or attrition explanation; its numerical size cannot be measured without the data.
findings.how_to_check: Before line 225 of `clean_FS_and_combineV5_nber.do`, count records satisfying the four-name condition, then separately count those with `age==.` and `age_fs==.`. Reconcile these losses alongside the two later merges to the 51,036,859 headline denominator.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove the unused `age_fs` completeness condition from the headline-data construction or disclose it and include its record loss in the sample reconciliation. Add assertions recording attrition after each eligibility condition and merge.

verified_clean.item: The headline linkage and middle-initial percentages reproduce the generated table
verified_clean.evidence: `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:139-209` computes before/after means and relative changes and writes the table directly. The resulting cells in `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/figures/avg_performance_allstates.tex:7-11` support the paper’s 119%, 28%, 8%, and 1% figures.

verified_clean.item: Blank middle initials cannot be counted as validating links
verified_clean.evidence: `CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:67-78` defines `validated_before` and `validated_after` only when both middle initials are nonempty and the record is linked.

verified_clean.item: Discordant-record model-versus-human categories form an asserted partition without conditioning on model success
verified_clean.evidence: `CODE/compute_model_agreement_on_discordant.do:109-137` requires all four human fields, assigns incomplete model output its own category, and exits if the category counts do not equal the denominator.

verified_clean.item: The paper appropriately distinguishes consensus-label agreement from adjudicated accuracy in the model-performance section
verified_clean.evidence: `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:274-280` explicitly identifies shared-error and legibility selection and says the values are agreement rates, not verified accuracy.

verified_clean.item: The paper does not interpret greater FamilySearch agreement as proof FamilySearch is more accurate
verified_clean.evidence: `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:298-305` describes the 14%/52% split as resemblance, lists normalization and ditto-resolution explanations, and says adjudication would be required.

verified_clean.item: Quoted genealogical-validation counts and rates match the included artifacts
verified_clean.evidence: The values at `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:556-571` match `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/figures/deaglan_abe_jw_restricted.tex:10-18` and `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/figures/deaglan_hlink_restricted.tex:10-18`, including the increases in contradicted counts that the prose discloses.

verified_clean.item: The draft discloses non-one-to-one match-rate numerators and differing algorithm denominators
verified_clean.evidence: `D:/repos/6638fa0fd89fbec05130caeb/DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:574-578` explicitly states that linked-pair counts are not unique-person linkage rates and that ABE/Jaro-Winkler and HLINK use different populations.

review_limits: The census, transcription, model-prediction, and linkage datasets reside outside the repository, so reported values and inferred attrition could not be recomputed.
The machine-learning training and evaluation implementation is absent from `CODE/`; model architecture, split integrity, and performance scoring could not be audited.

The programs generating the Deaglan ABE, Jaro-Winkler, and HLINK artifacts are outside the review target. Their included tables and provenance notes were checked against the paper, but the underlying link-level computation was not rerun.

All files under `CODE/` were inventoried and searched. Central construction and claim-producing analysis scripts were read directly; large generated IPUMS import dictionaries and value-label blocks were not treated as substantive analysis logic.

The FamilySearch-age finding is marked likely because the source shows the restriction, but unseen data are needed to determine whether it excludes any records and how much of the reported denominator difference it explains.
